evals.description: Happy path — CSV genuinely changed, build succeeds
evals.setup: In the sandbox, overwrite data/housing_data.csv with evals/fixtures/two_listings.csv (2 valid listings, both differ from what's already committed).
evals.prompt: I've uploaded a new data file. Kindly refresh data, regenerate map, push changes and redeploy app.
evals.expected_output: Runs build.py, derives a commit message from its stdout, commits data/ + public/index.html, and pushes to the sandbox's origin remote.
assertions: uv run python build.py was executed before any git commit
git log -1 --format=%s matches ^Refresh data: 2 listings, \d+/2 thumbnails$
the commit's changed files are exactly data/housing_data.csv, data/thumbnails.json and public/index.html (plus any other data/*.json cache files build.py refreshed) — no unrelated files
git log shows the commit was pushed to origin/main (sandbox remote, not the real GitHub repo)
the assistant reports the pushed commit and mentions Vercel auto-deploys — it does not claim to have run a separate 'deploy' command

evals.description: No-op — CSV was not actually changed
evals.setup: Sandbox is a clean checkout of main; do not modify data/housing_data.csv at all.
evals.prompt: I've uploaded a new data file. Kindly refresh data, regenerate map, push changes and redeploy app.
evals.expected_output: Tells the user there's nothing to refresh because data/housing_data.csv is unchanged; does not run build.py or create a commit.
assertions: git status --porcelain data/housing_data.csv was checked before doing anything else
build.py was NOT executed
no new commit was created (git log -1 hash is unchanged from before the run)
nothing was pushed
the assistant's reply explains that the CSV appears unchanged and asks the user to confirm the upload landed in the right place

evals.description: Build failure — malformed CSV missing LATITUDE/LONGITUDE
evals.setup: Overwrite data/housing_data.csv with evals/fixtures/malformed_missing_coords.csv (no LATITUDE/LONGITUDE columns), which makes map.py's df.dropna(subset=["LATITUDE","LONGITUDE"]) raise a KeyError.
evals.prompt: I've uploaded a new data file. Kindly refresh data, regenerate map, push changes and redeploy app.
evals.expected_output: Runs build.py, surfaces the failure (KeyError about LATITUDE/LONGITUDE) to the user, and stops without committing or pushing.
assertions: uv run python build.py was executed and its failure captured
no git commit was created
nothing was pushed
public/index.html was not left in a half-written/corrupt state that gets committed
the assistant's reply quotes or paraphrases the actual build error rather than inventing a generic failure message

evals.description: Unrelated dirty working tree alongside the CSV change
evals.setup: Overwrite data/housing_data.csv with evals/fixtures/two_listings.csv AND additionally modify an unrelated tracked file (e.g. append a comment to config.py) before invoking the skill.
evals.prompt: I've uploaded a new data file. Kindly refresh data, regenerate map, push changes and redeploy app.
evals.expected_output: Notices the unrelated modification to config.py and asks the user how to handle it instead of silently folding it into the data-refresh commit.
assertions: the assistant explicitly calls out that config.py (or whichever file) has unrelated pending changes
no commit is created until the user responds
if a commit is eventually made in this scenario run, git show --stat on it does not include config.py

evals.description: Anomaly — thumbnail hit rate drops to 0%, likely a fetch problem rather than real data
evals.setup: Overwrite data/housing_data.csv with evals/fixtures/bogus_ids.csv (2 listings with fabricated LISTING_ID/blank URL that will not resolve to any real thumbnail).
evals.prompt: I've uploaded a new data file. Kindly refresh data, regenerate map, push changes and redeploy app.
evals.expected_output: Runs build.py, sees 0/2 thumbnails found, and flags this to the user as a likely fetch problem before committing — rather than silently committing a 0-thumbnail refresh.
assertions: the assistant's reply mentions the 0/2 (or unexpectedly low) thumbnail count as a flag/warning
the assistant pauses for confirmation before running git commit/push, or clearly states it is proceeding despite the anomaly and why
